week_in_history.narrative:
This one gets the flashback nod because it's the closest Week 4 margin in league history — 1.82 points, the kind of gap you could close by shifting your beer gut on the couch. Brian Harris scraped past John Schauder, 108.02 to 106.20, and while the final score suggests a coin-flip, what came after tells you everything about who actually deserved it.

Brian limped through the rest of the season at a shrug-worthy 5-5, but it was enough to sneak into the playoffs, where he promptly got bounced in the quarterfinal — proof that surviving Week 4 by less than two points doesn't buy you a trophy, just a slightly longer year of disappointment.

John, meanwhile, took this heartbreaker and turned it into a full-blown identity crisis, cratering to 3-6 the rest of the way and missing the playoffs entirely. A 1.82-point loss shouldn't define a season, but John made sure it was just the opening act of his collapse.

weekly_recap.previous_weekend: Brian Kleinhenz pulled off a legit heist here, closing out the final game of the week to erase a lead Eddie McCumiskey held all day — Eddie was up 110.02 to 76.9 before Brian's roster caught fire late, stealing it away 113.98 to 110.02, a brutal 3.96-point gut punch. This was their fifth all-time meeting, and Brian now leads the series 3-2, adding another notch to a rivalry Eddie can't seem to solve. Hunter Henry's 25.0 points fueled the comeback, while Troy Franklin's quiet 1.8 points barely registered as a blemish. Eddie's own James Cook III racked up 21.3 points, but it means nothing next to the CeeDee Lamb-shaped hole in his lineup — a flat zero that sank him, especially with Khalil Shakir sitting on his bench posting 12.5 points that would've won the game outright. Add in a career winning percentage of 58.1% against Brian's 63.3%, and this loss fits Eddie's pattern perfectly.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: Call this one a genuine top-6 showdown that turned into a horror movie for Brian Harris, who was actually leading 101.18 to 97.20 heading into the final game of the week before Greg Wigton's last lineup card came in and torched him anyway, 124.22 to 101.18. That's a 23.04-point margin manufactured in the final inning, the fantasy equivalent of Brian passing out in the commissioner's driveway again — this time from a Bengals D/ST that finished at -1.0 points and actively subtracted from his score. Meanwhile Lamar Jackson dropped 27.02 points for Greg, who now leads their all-time series 3-2... wait, Brian leads that 3-2, but he won't enjoy this one bit.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week: Undefeated collides with undefeated as 2nd ranked Kleinhenz's Eye on 2026 rolls into 1st ranked Jay Nelson's High Quality H2O, both sitting pretty at 3 and 0 with matching zeroes in the loss column and matching swagger in their strut. Nelson's squad is averaging 101.76 points a game this season against Kleinhenz's 94.39, and his power score of 20.5 dwarfs Kleinhenz's 15.5 like a Costco water jug next to a Dixie cup — fitting, given the team name. Kleinhenz, meanwhile, is presumably drafting another unhinged trade proposal in his spare time, the kind of lopsided offer that makes league mates check their rosters for a hidden camera. Nelson, the league's trusted commissioner, gets to enforce the very rules Kleinhenz keeps trying to bend into pretzels. Their all-time series sits tied 1-1, so someone leaves this one actually trusting the process, and someone leaves questioning every trade text they've ever sent.
